# Ada Lovelace Institute

> An independent research institute dedicated to ensuring data and AI systems work for people through evidence-based policy research, public participation, and ethical governance frameworks.

The Ada Lovelace Institute conducts rigorous research on AI governance, data ethics, and digital regulation across the UK and Europe. Their work bridges public participation, policy analysis, and emerging technology practice to shape equitable AI policy and implementation.

## Key Topics

- AI governance
- AI regulation
- Data ethics
- Public participation
- Data governance
- EU regulation
- GDPR
- AI transcription tools
- Digital governance
- Policy research
- Algorithmic harm
- Public trust
- AI policy
- Vulnerable populations
- Digital omnibus

- [Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org): Homepage for independent research institute ensuring data and AI works for people

- [Our work | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/our-work): Overview of research projects and methodologies on data governance and AI ethics

## Research Teams & Practice Areas

- [Law & Policy | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/our-work/how-we-work/ai-law-policy): Law & Policy team overview examining AI and data regulation, governance, and policymaking
- [Public Participation & Research | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/our-work/how-we-work/public-participation-research): Public participation research approach ensuring affected voices shape policy and practices
- [Emerging Technology & Industry Practice | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/our-work/how-we-work/emerging-technology-industry-practice): Research practice ensuring equitable technology benefits and prevention of potential harms

## Policy Briefings & Research

- [Great (public) expectations | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/policy-briefing/great-expectations): Policy briefing on public attitudes toward AI governance and regulatory expectations
- [The regulation of delegation | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/policy-briefing/the-regulation-of-delegation): Policy briefing on UK regulation of AI advisers, agents, and companions
- [Scribe and prejudice? | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/report/scribe-and-prejudice): Research report on AI transcription tools in social care and implementation guidance
- [Smarter, not simpler, rules: five questions on the EU Digital Omnibus | Ada Lovelace Institute](https://www.adalovelaceinstitute.org/blog/smarter-rules-questions-on-digital-omnibus): Analysis of EU Digital Omnibus regulation tensions and digital governance commitments
